title: Traffic Control
description: Bandwidth policies, host fairness and resource pressure in one workspace.
enableHint: Limits are disabled by default. The scheduler still protects lightweight TUN queues.
unitHint: Rates use decimal Mbps (1 Mbps = 125,000 bytes/s). Zero means unlimited; burst 0 uses the engine default for limited rates.
noProfiles: No profiles yet. Add one to assign inbound or routing policies.
bindingOptionsUnavailable: Could not load all binding choices. Check the backend connection and retry.
saved: Traffic Control configuration saved and activated.
diagnosticsHint: Aggregate counters only. These are not per-user bandwidth counters or physical-wire measurements.
truncated: Scope list truncated to protect diagnostics cardinality.
statusUnavailable: Traffic Control diagnostics are unavailable. Check the paired backend version.
limitations: Host isolation applies to the lightweight TUN output path. Per-user authenticated fairness, CAKE and physical WAN shaping are not claimed here.

resources.title: Identity resource policies
resources.help: Apply bandwidth, session budgets and byte quotas across a user’s listeners and devices. Global, inbound and route limits also apply.
resources.overrideHelp: An explicit user policy replaces this default. Group and credential constraints still apply.
resources.groupHelp: Shared bandwidth and quotas cover the entire group. Individual bandwidth and session limits apply separately to each member. All matching groups apply; individual rates, bursts and resource caps use the most restrictive values.
resources.limitsHelp: Zero is unlimited. Creation and packet bursts default to at least one event when a rate is set. Active sessions are retained when lowering a limit; new sessions wait for capacity.
resources.quotaHelp: Exact decimal bytes; zero is unlimited for that direction. Daily resets at 00:00 UTC; monthly resets on the first day at 00:00 UTC. Usage counts admitted application bytes. Restart recovery may conservatively charge unused durable credit.
resources.periodResetConfirm: Changing the period creates a new quota ID and starts a new budget. Historical usage is retained. Continue?
resources.block_new: Block new sessions and pause existing traffic until reset
resources.invalidThresholds: Enter up to ten distinct whole percentages from 1 to 100.
resources.invalidBytes: Enter an unsigned decimal byte count up to 9223372036854775807.
resources.discardConfirm: Reload the active resource policy and discard unsaved edits?
resources.activateConfirm: Activate this resource policy for existing streams and later datagrams?
resources.requestFailed: Resource policy request failed. Your draft is retained.
resources.conflict: The active resource policy changed. Your draft is retained; reload before saving again.
resources.status: {{windows}} quota windows · {{pending}} pending writes · {{denied}} denied · {{failures}} persistence failures · {{refreshFailures}} refresh failures · {{dropped}} dropped alerts · {{alertPending}} pending alerts · {{alertFailures}} alert persistence failures
resources.usageHelp: These are active limits, not an unsaved policy draft. All listed scopes apply; shared group bandwidth covers every member. Listener and route profiles may add further caps. Remaining quota excludes in-flight reservations. Recovery charges in different directions are independent and may not sum.
resources.disabled: Identity resource enforcement is disabled. Global traffic controls can still apply.
resources.persistenceWarning: Quota or alert persistence has reported failures since startup. Some alert history may be incomplete.
resources.noQuotas: No byte quota is configured for this user.
resources.alertHelp: Thresholds alert once per quota window. History retains the latest 10,000 alerts across the instance; overload or persistence failures may drop events. Group alerts are visible to current members.

reasons.quota_credit_pending: Quota credit or window update pending
